**Why it wins:** Unlike many portable power stations under $1,000, the AC200L combines roughly 2kWh of storage with a dedicated 30-amp-style RV outlet. That makes it particularly practical for running an RV refrigerator, lights, water pump, and occasional small appliances without relying on multiple extension cords.

The 2,400W inverter provides about 20 amps at 120V, however—not a full 30 amps of RV shore power. It also isn't a practical solution for running rooftop air conditioning continuously. <Cite refs={["turn154223view0"]}/>

## What I'd buy

For **multi-day RV boondocking**, I'd choose the **BLUETTI AC200L** because its battery capacity, inverter output, solar charging, and RV outlet are a strong combination for the price.

For weekend camping where weight matters more, I'd consider the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2.

One important caveat: a 2kWh power station generally won't power a typical RV air conditioner overnight. For longer off-grid stays, solar recharging and careful refrigerator power management are essential.

The supplied results list an AC200L promotional price of **$854.05 with code AFF5OFF** through an affiliate checkout link. The model is also nearing the end of its product life, so confirm availability and warranty terms before purchasing.

<Link url="https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv" title="Read the detailed RV power station comparison"/>

**Bottom line:** The BLUETTI AC200L is my pick under $1,000 for RV boondocking, especially if you want to connect directly to your RV's electrical system.
